name: Lice-silencing fish feed
subtitle: salmon feed that disarms sea lice

effects.effect: double-stranded RNA silences the matching gene

effect: double-stranded RNA silences the matching gene
how: Sea lice are the biggest single cost in salmon farming and the main reason farms dose fish with chemicals the lice keep growing resistant to. Lice feed on the skin and mucus of the fish, which means anything in that mucus reaches them. Feed pellets carrying double-stranded RNA that matches a louse gene, taken up by the fish and passed into the mucus layer, would silence that gene in the parasite while the fish's own genes, which do not match, are untouched.
obstacle: Getting intact RNA through a fish's digestion and out into the mucus in useful amounts is unproven.
why: Injected RNA kills lice in the lab; the delivery route through feed is the gap.
real: RNAi works in the salmon louse by immersion and injection (up to ~97% knockdown) and a patent describes salmon feed coated with dsRNA-expressing algae against louse COPB2, but no demonstrated louse-count reduction from oral dsRNA feed was found.
